NASB.1: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, according to Shigionoth.
NASB.2: LORD, I have heard the report about You [and] I fear. O LORD, revive Your work in the midst of the years, In the midst of the years make it known; In wrath remember mercy.
NASB.3: God comes from Teman, And the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His splendor covers the heavens, And the earth is full of His praise.
NASB.4: [His] radiance is like the sunlight; He has rays [flashing] from His hand, And there is the hiding of His power.
NASB.5: Before Him goes pestilence, And plague comes after Him.
NASB.6: He stood and surveyed the earth; He looked and startled the nations. Yes, the perpetual mountains were shattered, The ancient hills collapsed. His ways are everlasting.
NASB.7: I saw the tents of Cushan under distress, The tent curtains of the land of Midian were trembling.
NASB.8: Did the LORD rage against the rivers, Or [was] Your anger against the rivers, Or [was] Your wrath against the sea, That You rode on Your horses, On Your chariots of salvation?
NASB.9: Your bow was made bare, The rods of chastisement were sworn. Selah. You cleaved the earth with rivers.
NASB.10: The mountains saw You [and] quaked; The downpour of waters swept by. The deep uttered forth its voice, It lifted high its hands.
NASB.11: Sun [and] moon stood in their places; They went away at the light of Your arrows, At the radiance of Your gleaming spear.
NASB.12: In indignation You marched through the earth; In anger You trampled the nations.
NASB.13: You went forth for the salvation of Your people, For the salvation of Your anointed. You struck the head of the house of the evil To lay him open from thigh to neck. Selah.
NASB.14: You pierced with his own spears The head of his throngs. They stormed in to scatter us; Their exultation [was] like those Who devour the oppressed in secret.
NASB.15: You trampled on the sea with Your horses, On the surge of many waters.
NASB.16: I heard and my inward parts trembled, At the sound my lips quivered. Decay enters my bones, And in my place I tremble. Because I must wait quietly for the day of distress, For the people to arise [who] will invade us.
NASB.17: Though the fig tree should not blossom And there be no fruit on the vines, [Though] the yield of the olive should fail And the fields produce no food, Though the flock should be cut off from the fold And there be no cattle in the stalls,
NASB.18: Yet I will exult in the LORD, I will rejoice in the God of my salvation.
NASB.19: The Lord GOD is my strength, And He has made my feet like hinds' [feet], And makes me walk on my high places. For the choir director, on my stringed instruments.

ESV.1: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, according to Shigionoth.
ESV.2: O LORD, I have heard the report of you, and your work, O LORD, do I fear. In the midst of the years revive it; in the midst of the years make it known; in wrath remember mercy.
ESV.3: God came from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah His splendor covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.
ESV.4: His brightness was like the light; rays flashed from his hand; and there he veiled his power.
ESV.5: Before him went pestilence, and plague followed at his heels.
ESV.6: He stood and measured the earth; he looked and shook the nations; then the eternal mountains were scattered; the everlasting hills sank low. His were the everlasting ways.
ESV.7: I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction; the curtains of the land of Midian did tremble.
ESV.8: Was your wrath against the rivers, O LORD? Was your anger against the rivers, or your indignation against the sea, when you rode on your horses, on your chariot of salvation?
ESV.9: You stripped the sheath from your bow, calling for many arrows. Selah You split the earth with rivers.
ESV.10: The mountains saw you and writhed; the raging waters swept on; the deep gave forth its voice; it lifted its hands on high.
ESV.11: The sun and moon stood still in their place at the light of your arrows as they sped, at the flash of your glittering spear.
ESV.12: You marched through the earth in fury; you threshed the nations in anger.
ESV.13: You went out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of your anointed. You crushed the head of the house of the wicked, laying him bare from thigh to neck. Selah
ESV.14: You pierced with his own arrows the heads of his warriors, who came like a whirlwind to scatter me, rejoicing as if to devour the poor in secret.
ESV.15: You trampled the sea with your horses, the surging of mighty waters.
ESV.16: I hear, and my body trembles; my lips quiver at the sound; rottenness enters into my bones; my legs tremble beneath me. Yet I will quietly wait for the day of trouble to come upon people who invade us.
ESV.17: Though the fig tree should not blossom, nor fruit be on the vines, the produce of the olive fail and the fields yield no food, the flock be cut off from the fold and there be no herd in the stalls,
ESV.18: yet I will rejoice in the LORD; I will take joy in the God of my salvation.
ESV.19: GOD, the Lord, is my strength; he makes my feet like the deer's; he makes me tread on my high places.  To the choirmaster: with stringed  instruments.

NKJV.1: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, on Shigionoth.
NKJV.2: O LORD, I have heard Your speech and was afraid; O LORD, revive Your work in the midst of the years! In the midst of the years make it known; In wrath remember mercy.
NKJV.3: God came from Teman, The Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah His glory covered the heavens, And the earth was full of His praise.
NKJV.4: His brightness was like the light; He had rays flashing from His hand, And there His power was hidden.
NKJV.5: Before Him went pestilence, And fever followed at His feet.
NKJV.6: He stood and measured the earth; He looked and startled the nations. And the everlasting mountains were scattered, The perpetual hills bowed. His ways are everlasting.
NKJV.7: I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction; The curtains of the land of Midian trembled.
NKJV.8: O LORD, were You displeased with the rivers, Was Your anger against the rivers, Was Your wrath against the sea, That You rode on Your horses, Your chariots of salvation?
NKJV.9: Your bow was made quite ready; Oaths were sworn over Your arrows. Selah You divided the earth with rivers.
NKJV.10: The mountains saw You and trembled; The overflowing of the water passed by. The deep uttered its voice, And lifted its hands on high.
NKJV.11: The sun and moon stood still in their habitation; At the light of Your arrows they went, At the shining of Your glittering spear.
NKJV.12: You marched through the land in indignation; You trampled the nations in anger.
NKJV.13: You went forth for the salvation of Your people, For salvation with Your Anointed. You struck the head from the house of the wicked, By laying bare from foundation to neck. Selah
NKJV.14: You thrust through with his own arrows The head of his villages. They came out like a whirlwind to scatter me; Their rejoicing was like feasting on the poor in secret.
NKJV.15: You walked through the sea with Your horses, Through the heap of great waters.
NKJV.16: When I heard, my body trembled; My lips quivered at the voice; Rottenness entered my bones; And I trembled in myself, That I might rest in the day of trouble. When he comes up to the people, He will invade them with his troops.
NKJV.17: Though the fig tree may not blossom, Nor fruit be on the vines; Though the labor of the olive may fail, And the fields yield no food; Though the flock may be cut off from the fold, And there be no herd in the stalls—
NKJV.18: Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation.
NKJV.19: The LORD God is my strength; He will make my feet like deer’s feet, And He will make me walk on my high hills. To the Chief Musician. With my stringed instruments.

WEB.1: A prayer of Habakkuk, the prophet, set to victorious music.
WEB.2: Yahweh, I have heard of your fame. I stand in awe of your deeds, Yahweh. Renew your work in the middle of the years. In the middle of the years make it known. In wrath, you remember mercy.
WEB.3: God came from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered the heavens, and his praise filled the earth.
WEB.4: His splendor is like the sunrise. Rays shine from his hand, where his power is hidden.
WEB.5: Plague went before him, and pestilence followed his feet.
WEB.6: He stood, and shook the earth. He looked, and made the nations tremble. The ancient mountains were crumbled. The age-old hills collapsed. His ways are eternal.
WEB.7: I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction. The dwellings of the land of Midian trembled.
WEB.8: Was Yahweh displeased with the rivers? Was your anger against the rivers, or your wrath against the sea, that you rode on your horses, on your chariots of salvation?
WEB.9: You uncovered your bow. You called for your sworn arrows. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.
WEB.10: The mountains saw you, and were afraid. The storm of waters passed by. The deep roared and lifted up its hands on high.
WEB.11: The sun and moon stood still in the sky, at the light of your arrows as they went, at the shining of your glittering spear.
WEB.12: You marched through the land in wrath. You threshed the nations in anger.
WEB.13: You went out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of your anointed. You crushed the head of the land of wickedness. You stripped them head to foot. Selah.
WEB.14: You pierced the heads of his warriors with their own spears. They came as a whirlwind to scatter me, gloating as if to devour the wretched in secret.
WEB.15: You trampled the sea with your horses, churning mighty waters.
WEB.16: I heard, and my body trembled. My lips quivered at the voice. Rottenness enters into my bones, and I tremble in my place, because I must wait quietly for the day of trouble, for the coming up of the people who invade us.
WEB.17: For though the fig tree doesn’t flourish, nor fruit be in the vines; the labor of the olive fails, the fields yield no food; the flocks are cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls:
WEB.18: yet I will rejoice in Yahweh. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!
WEB.19: Yahweh, the Lord,  is my strength. He makes my feet like deer’s feet, and enables me to go in high places.  For the music director, on my stringed instruments.

NLT.1: This prayer was sung by the prophet Habakkuk :
NLT.2:
I have heard all about you, LORD.
I am filled with awe by your amazing works.
In this time of our deep need,
help us again as you did in years gone by.
And in your anger,
remember your mercy.
NLT.3:
I see God moving across the deserts from Edom,
the Holy One coming from Mount Paran.
His brilliant splendor fills the heavens,
and the earth is filled with his praise.
NLT.4:
His coming is as brilliant as the sunrise.
Rays of light flash from his hands,
where his awesome power is hidden.
NLT.5:
Pestilence marches before him;
plague follows close behind.
NLT.6:
When he stops, the earth shakes.
When he looks, the nations tremble.
He shatters the everlasting mountains
and levels the eternal hills.
He is the Eternal One!
NLT.7:
I see the people of Cushan in distress,
and the nation of Midian trembling in terror.
NLT.8:
Was it in anger, LORD, that you struck the rivers
and parted the sea?
Were you displeased with them?
No, you were sending your chariots of salvation!
NLT.9:
You brandished your bow
and your quiver of arrows.
You split open the earth with flowing rivers.
NLT.10:
The mountains watched and trembled.
Onward swept the raging waters.
The mighty deep cried out,
lifting its hands in submission.
NLT.11:
The sun and moon stood still in the sky
as your brilliant arrows flew
and your glittering spear flashed.
NLT.12:
You marched across the land in anger
and trampled the nations in your fury.
NLT.13:
You went out to rescue your chosen people,
to save your anointed ones.
You crushed the heads of the wicked
and stripped their bones from head to toe.
NLT.14:
With his own weapons,
you destroyed the chief of those
who rushed out like a whirlwind,
thinking Israel would be easy prey.
NLT.15:
You trampled the sea with your horses,
and the mighty waters piled high.
NLT.16:
I trembled inside when I heard this;
my lips quivered with fear.
My legs gave way beneath me,
and I shook in terror.
I will wait quietly for the coming day
when disaster will strike the people who invade us.
NLT.17:
Even though the fig trees have no blossoms,
and there are no grapes on the vines;
even though the olive crop fails,
and the fields lie empty and barren;
even though the flocks die in the fields,
and the cattle barns are empty,
NLT.18:
yet I will rejoice in the LORD!
I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!
NLT.19:
The Sovereign LORD is my strength!
He makes me as surefooted as a deer,
able to tread upon the heights.
(For the choir director: This prayer is to be accompanied by stringed instruments.)

AMP.1: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, set to wild and enthusiastic music.
AMP.2:
O LORD, I have heard the report about You and I fear.
O LORD, revive Your work in the midst of the years,
In the midst of the years make it known;
In wrath [earnestly] remember compassion and love.
AMP.3:
God [approaching from Sinai] comes from Teman (Edom),
And the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah ( pause, and calmly think of that).
His splendor and majesty covers the heavens
And the earth is full of His praise.
AMP.4:
His brightness is like the sunlight;
He has [bright] rays flashing from His hand,
And there [in the sunlike splendor] is the hiding place of His power.
AMP.5:
Before Him goes the pestilence [of judgment as in Egypt],
And [the burning] plague [of condemnation] follows at His feet [as in Sennacherib's army].
AMP.6:
He stood and measured the earth;
He looked and startled the nations,
Yes, the eternal mountains were shattered,
The ancient hills bowed low and collapsed.
His ways are eternal.
AMP.7:
I [Habakkuk, in my vision] saw the tents of Cushan under distress;
The tent curtains of the land of Midian were trembling.
AMP.8:
Did the LORD rage against the rivers,
Or was Your anger against the rivers,
Or was Your wrath against the [Red] Sea,
That You rode on Your horses,
On Your chariots of salvation?
AMP.9:
Your bow was made bare;
The rods of chastisement were sworn. Selah (pause, calmly think of that).
You split the earth with rivers [bringing waters to dry places].
AMP.10:
The mountains saw You and [they] trembled and writhed [as if in pain];
The downpour of waters swept by [as a deluge].
The deep uttered its voice and raged,
It lifted its hands high.
AMP.11:
The sun and moon stood in their places [as before Joshua];
They went away at the light of Your [swift] arrows,
At the radiance and gleam of Your glittering spear.
AMP.12:
In indignation You marched through the earth;
In anger You trampled and threshed the nations.
AMP.13:
You went forth for the salvation of Your people,
For the salvation and rescue of Your anointed [people Israel].
You struck the head from the house of the wicked
To lay him open from the thigh to the neck. Selah (pause, and calmly think of that).
AMP.14:
With the enemy's own spears, You pierced
The head of his hordes.
They stormed out to scatter us,
Rejoicing like those
Who secretly devour the oppressed [of Israel].
AMP.15:
You have trampled on the sea with Your horses,
On the surge of many waters.
AMP.16:
I heard and my whole inner self trembled;
My lips quivered at the sound.
Decay and rottenness enter my bones,
And I tremble in my place.
Because I must wait quietly for the day of distress,
For the people to arise who will invade and attack us.
AMP.17:
Though the fig tree does not blossom
And there is no fruit on the vines,
Though the yield of the olive fails
And the fields produce no food,
Though the flock is cut off from the fold
And there are no cattle in the stalls,
AMP.18:
Yet I will [choose to] rejoice in the LORD;
I will [choose to] shout in exultation in the [victorious] God of my salvation!
AMP.19:
The Lord GOD is my strength [my source of courage, my invincible army];
He has made my feet [steady and sure] like hinds' feet
And makes me walk [forward with spiritual confidence] on my high places [of challenge and responsibility].
For the choir director, on my stringed instruments.

NRSVCE.1: A prayer of the prophet Habakkuk according to Shigionoth.
NRSVCE.2:
O LORD, I have heard of your renown,
and I stand in awe, O LORD, of your work.
In our own time revive it;
in our own time make it known;
in wrath may you remember mercy.
NRSVCE.3:
God came from Teman,
the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah
His glory covered the heavens,
and the earth was full of his praise.
NRSVCE.4:
The brightness was like the sun;
rays came forth from his hand,
where his power lay hidden.
NRSVCE.5:
Before him went pestilence,
and plague followed close behind.
NRSVCE.6:
He stopped and shook the earth;
he looked and made the nations tremble.
The eternal mountains were shattered;
along his ancient pathways
the everlasting hills sank low.
NRSVCE.7:
I saw the tents of Cushan under affliction;
the tent-curtains of the land of Midian trembled.
NRSVCE.8:
Was your wrath against the rivers, O LORD?
Or your anger against the rivers,
or your rage against the sea,
when you drove your horses,
your chariots to victory?
NRSVCE.9:
You brandished your naked bow,
sated were the arrows at your command. Selah
You split the earth with rivers.
NRSVCE.10:
The mountains saw you, and writhed;
a torrent of water swept by;
the deep gave forth its voice.
The sun raised high its hands;
NRSVCE.11:
the moon stood still in its exalted place,
at the light of your arrows speeding by,
at the gleam of your flashing spear.
NRSVCE.12:
In fury you trod the earth,
in anger you trampled nations.
NRSVCE.13:
You came forth to save your people,
to save your anointed.
You crushed the head of the wicked house,
laying it bare from foundation to roof. Selah
NRSVCE.14:
You pierced with their own arrows the head of his warriors,
who came like a whirlwind to scatter us,
gloating as if ready to devour the poor who were in hiding.
NRSVCE.15:
You trampled the sea with your horses,
churning the mighty waters.
NRSVCE.16:
I hear, and I tremble within;
my lips quiver at the sound.
Rottenness enters into my bones,
and my steps tremble beneath me.
I wait quietly for the day of calamity
to come upon the people who attack us.
NRSVCE.17:
Though the fig tree does not blossom,
and no fruit is on the vines;
though the produce of the olive fails,
and the fields yield no food;
though the flock is cut off from the fold,
and there is no herd in the stalls,
NRSVCE.18:
yet I will rejoice in the LORD;
I will exult in the God of my salvation.
NRSVCE.19:
GOD, the Lord, is my strength;
he makes my feet like the feet of a deer,
and makes me tread upon the heights.
To the leader: with stringed instruments.

NIV.1:
Habakkuk’s Prayer
A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet. On shigionoth.
NIV.2:
Lord, I have heard of your fame;
I stand in awe of your deeds, O Lord.
Renew them in our day,
in our time make them known;
in wrath remember mercy.
NIV.3:
God came from Teman,
the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah
His glory covered the heavens
and his praise filled the earth.
NIV.4:
His splendor was like the sunrise;
rays flashed from his hand,
where his power was hidden.
NIV.5:
Plague went before him;
pestilence followed his steps.
NIV.6:
He stood, and shook the earth;
he looked, and made the nations tremble.
The ancient mountains crumbled
and the age-old hills collapsed.
His ways are eternal.
NIV.7:
I saw the tents of Cushan in distress,
the dwellings of Midian in anguish.
NIV.8:
Were you angry with the rivers, O Lord?
Was your wrath against the streams?
Did you rage against the sea
when you rode with your horses
and your victorious chariots?
NIV.9:
You uncovered your bow,
you called for many arrows. Selah
You split the earth with rivers;
NIV.10:
the mountains saw you and writhed.
Torrents of water swept by;
the deep roared
and lifted its waves on high.
NIV.11:
Sun and moon stood still in the heavens
at the glint of your flying arrows,
at the lightning of your flashing spear.
NIV.12:
In wrath you strode through the earth
and in anger you threshed the nations.
NIV.13:
You came out to deliver your people,
to save your anointed one.
You crushed the leader of the land of wickedness,
you stripped him from head to foot. Selah
NIV.14:
With his own spear you pierced his head
when his warriors stormed out to scatter us,
gloating as though about to devour
the wretched who were in hiding.
NIV.15:
You trampled the sea with your horses,
churning the great waters.
NIV.16:
I heard and my heart pounded,
my lips quivered at the sound;
decay crept into my bones,
and my legs trembled.
Yet I will wait patiently for the day of calamity
to come on the nation invading us.
NIV.17:
Though the fig tree does not bud
and there are no grapes on the vines,
though the olive crop fails
and the fields produce no food,
though there are no sheep in the pen
and no cattle in the stalls,
NIV.18:
yet I will rejoice in the Lord,
I will be joyful in God my Savior.
NIV.19:
The Sovereign Lord is my strength;
he makes my feet like the feet of a deer,
he enables me to go on the heights.
For the director of music. On my stringed instruments.

MSG.1: A prayer of the prophet Habakkuk, with orchestra:
MSG.2:
God, I've heard what our ancestors say about you,
and I'm stopped in my tracks, down on my knees.
Do among us what you did among them.
Work among us as you worked among them.
And as you bring judgment, as you surely must,
remember mercy.
MSG.3:
God's on his way again,
retracing the old salvation route,
Coming up from the south through Teman,
the Holy One from Mount Paran.
Skies are blazing with his splendor,
his praises sounding through the earth,
MSG.4:
His cloud-brightness like dawn, exploding, spreading,
forked-lightning shooting from his hand—
what power hidden in that fist!
MSG.5:
Plague marches before him,
pestilence at his heels!
MSG.6:
He stops. He shakes Earth.
He looks around. Nations tremble.
The age-old mountains fall to pieces;
ancient hills collapse like a spent balloon.
The paths God takes are older
than the oldest mountains and hills.
MSG.7:
I saw everyone worried, in a panic:
Old wilderness adversaries,
Cushan and Midian, were terrified,
hoping he wouldn't notice them.
MSG.8:
God, is it River you're mad at?
Angry at old River?
Were you raging at Sea when you rode
horse and chariot through to salvation?
MSG.9:
You unfurled your bow
and let loose a volley of arrows.
You split Earth with rivers.
MSG.10:
Mountains saw what was coming.
They twisted in pain.
Flood Waters poured in.
Ocean roared and reared huge waves.
MSG.11:
Sun and Moon stopped in their tracks.
Your flashing arrows stopped them,
your lightning-strike spears impaled them.
MSG.12:
Angry, you stomped through Earth.
Furious, you crushed the godless nations.
MSG.13:
You were out to save your people,
to save your specially chosen people.
You beat the stuffing
out of King Wicked,
Stripped him naked
from head to toe,
MSG.14:
Set his severed head on his own spear
and blew away his army.
Scattered they were to the four winds—
and ended up food for the sharks!
MSG.15:
You galloped through the Sea on your horses,
racing on the crest of the waves.
MSG.16:
When I heard it, my stomach did flips.
I stammered and stuttered.
My bones turned to water.
I staggered and stumbled.
I sit back and wait for Doomsday
to descend on our attackers.
MSG.17:
Though the cherry trees don't blossom
and the strawberries don't ripen,
Though the apples are worm-eaten
and the wheat fields stunted,
Though the sheep pens are sheepless
and the cattle barns empty,
MSG.18:
I'm singing joyful praise to God.
I'm turning cartwheels of joy to my Savior God.
MSG.19:
Counting on God's Rule to prevail,
I take heart and gain strength.
I run like a deer.
I feel like I'm king of the mountain!
(For congregational use, with a full orchestra.)

NET.1: This is a prayer of Habakkuk the prophet:
NET.2: LORD, I have heard the report of what you did; I am awed, LORD, by what you accomplished. In our time repeat those deeds; in our time reveal them again. But when you cause turmoil, remember to show us mercy!
NET.3: God comes from Teman, the sovereign one from Mount Paran. Selah. His splendor covers the skies, his glory fills the earth.
NET.4: He is as bright as lightning; a two-pronged lightning bolt flashes from his hand. This is the outward display of his power.
NET.5: Plague goes before him; pestilence marches right behind him.
NET.6: He takes his battle position and shakes the earth; with a mere look he frightens the nations. The ancient mountains disintegrate; the primeval hills are flattened. He travels on the ancient roads.
NET.7: I see the tents of Cushan overwhelmed by trouble; the tent curtains of the land of Midian are shaking.
NET.8: Is the LORD mad at the rivers? Are you angry with the rivers? Are you enraged at the sea? Is this why you climb into your horse-drawn chariots, your victorious chariots?
NET.9: Your bow is ready for action; you commission your arrows. Selah. You cause flash floods on the earth’s surface.
NET.10: When the mountains see you, they shake. The torrential downpour sweeps through. The great deep shouts out; it lifts its hands high.
NET.11: The sun and moon stand still in their courses; the flash of your arrows drives them away, the bright light of your lightning-quick spear.
NET.12: You furiously stomp on the earth, you angrily trample down the nations.
NET.13: You march out to deliver your people, to deliver your special servant. You strike the leader of the wicked nation, laying him open from the lower body to the neck. Selah.
NET.14: You pierce the heads of his warriors with a spear. They storm forward to scatter us; they shout with joy as if they were plundering the poor with no opposition.
NET.15: But you trample on the sea with your horses, on the surging, raging waters.
NET.16: I listened and my stomach churned; the sound made my lips quiver. My frame went limp, as if my bones were decaying, and I shook as I tried to walk. I long for the day of distress to come upon the people who attack us.
NET.17: When the fig tree does not bud, and there are no grapes on the vines; when the olive trees do not produce, and the fields yield no crops; when the sheep disappear from the pen, and there are no cattle in the stalls,
NET.18: I will rejoice because of the LORD; I will be happy because of the God who delivers me!
NET.19: The sovereign LORD is my source of strength. He gives me the agility of a deer; he enables me to negotiate the rugged terrain. (This prayer is for the song leader. It is to be accompanied by stringed instruments.)
